blocks.title: Free radical
blocks.text: A free radical is a species that has one or more unpaired electrons.

A simple example is the free chlorine atom, with the configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p5: in the 3p subshell two orbitals hold paired electrons and the third holds a single unpaired electron, shown by a dot after the symbol. Apart from single atoms, groups of atoms can also be free radicals, for example the hydroxyl radical OH and the methyl radical CH3.
